skill.name: opentargets-database
skill.description: Query the Open Targets Platform for target-disease associations, drug discovery evidence, tractability, safety, genetics, omics, and known drug data.
skill.summary: Explore Open Targets evidence for therapeutic target discovery and prioritization.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The confirmed issue is intentional network access to the public Open Targets GraphQL API. It can send user search terms, identifiers, and query variables to that service. Documentation URLs, markdown backticks, and GraphQL id fields are false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Document clearly that search terms, identifiers, GraphQL queries, and variables are sent to Open Targets. Warn users not to submit confidential hypotheses or unpublished project data.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded API endpoint in helper script
remediation.suggestion: Keep the endpoint restricted to the official Open Targets URL, or make it configurable with validation against approved Open Targets domains.

content.user_title: Analyze Open Targets Drug Discovery Data
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need structured target, disease, and drug evidence from Open Targets. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through GraphQL queries and interpretation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Search Open Targets targets, diseases, and drugs by name or identifier.
Retrieve target annotations including tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and associated diseases.
Query disease records with associated targets, therapeutic areas, and known drugs.
Collect target-disease evidence by evidence type and source.
Compare known drugs, mechanisms, trial phases, and indication data.
Use reference guides to interpret evidence scores and target annotations.
limitations: Requires internet access to the public Open Targets GraphQL API.
Not a replacement for clinical, regulatory, or primary literature review.
API examples are optimized for exploratory queries, not bulk analyses.
Open Targets scores are ranking metrics, not predictions of clinical success.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Targets for a Disease
use_cases.description: Find disease-associated targets, compare evidence types, and shortlist genes for deeper validation.

use_cases.title: Assess Target Safety and Tractability
use_cases.description: Review tractability, safety liabilities, expression, and genetic constraint before advancing a target.

use_cases.title: Map Repurposing Opportunities
use_cases.description: Identify known drugs, mechanisms, clinical phases, and related indications for repurposing research.

prompt_templates.title: Search for an Entity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Open Targets skill to find the Open Targets identifiers for BRCA1 and Alzheimer disease. Show the best matches and explain which IDs to use.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Target Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get_target_info for ENSG00000157764 and include disease associations. Summarize tractability, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and top disease links.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Evidence for Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: For disease EFO_0000249, identify top associated targets, retrieve evidence for three candidates, and compare the data types supporting each target.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Prioritization Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a target prioritization brief for a specified disease using genetic evidence, known drugs, safety, tractability, and evidence gaps. Include caveats and validation needs.

output_examples.input: Find IDs for BRCA1 and Alzheimer disease.
output_examples.output: BRCA1 maps to Ensembl gene ENSG00000012048. Alzheimer disease maps to EFO_0000249. Use these identifiers for target and disease queries.

output_examples.input: Summarize BRAF target information for prioritization.
output_examples.output: The response highlights approved symbol, tractability by modality, safety liabilities, genetic constraint, and the strongest disease associations for review.

output_examples.input: Compare known drugs for a disease indication.
output_examples.output: The analysis lists drugs, targets, mechanisms, clinical phases, trial status, and notes where evidence supports repurposing hypotheses.

best_practices: Start with official Open Targets identifiers before querying evidence or associations.
Review evidence type breakdowns instead of relying only on the overall score.
Cite Open Targets and verify critical claims in primary sources.
anti_patterns: Treating association scores as clinical success probabilities.
Running large systematic analyses through the exploratory API instead of downloads or BigQuery.
Making therapeutic decisions without manual evidence and safety review.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The Open Targets GraphQL API is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: What data does it send externally?
faq.answer: It sends search terms, identifiers, GraphQL queries, and query variables to the Open Targets API.

faq.question: Can it analyze many targets at once?
faq.answer: It is best for exploratory queries. Use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery for large-scale analysis.

faq.question: Can it replace expert review?
faq.answer: No. It supports research workflows, but clinical and scientific decisions require expert validation.

faq.question: Which identifiers should I use?
faq.answer: Use Ensembl gene IDs for targets, EFO IDs for diseases, and ChEMBL IDs for drugs.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
